title: Signed erasure record, tombstone and restore receipt v1
description: The machine-readable form of the append-only erasure log, the tombstones it produces and the receipt a restore writes. docs/privacy/ERASURE_AND_KEY_DESTRUCTION.md is the normative owner and ADR-022 is the reasoning. A record proves which key was destroyed and that the log has not been rewritten. It does not prove that no copy of the key exists anywhere, and no mechanism can.

chain_sequence.description: Dense and unique from 1. The chain is the tamper evidence: a removed record leaves a gap and a rewritten one breaks every digest after it.

key_commitment.description: SHA-256 over key_id concatenated with the key material, taken before destruction and retained after it. A candidate key can be tested against it; it cannot be inverted, because a 256-bit uniformly random preimage is not searchable.

affected_generation_count.description: How many sealed generations hold an entry for this domain. Those generations are no longer rebuildable from source claims, because the erasure deletes them.

record_digest.description: SHA-256 over the deterministic CBOR encoding of the record body, under the Core Deterministic Encoding profile D-191 fixes.

cose_sign1.description: Base64url COSE_Sign1 over record_digest, Ed25519, algorithm identifier -19 per D-190, verified under the ZIP-215 rules D-192 pins.

journal_mirrored_at.description: When the record reached the append-only journal held outside the database backup set. The participant is not acknowledged before this is durable.

erasure_record_id.description: Present exactly on an erasure-domain tombstone. The other classes record a deletion that destroyed no key.

traffic_admitted_at.description: Never earlier than reapply_completed_at, which packages/schemas/planning-schema.sql enforces as a check constraint. Between the restore and the reapply the cluster holds live keys for domains that were erased after the restore point; it serves no application traffic during that interval, and the interval is not zero.
